legend: Hallmarks of intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma are well-demarcated microscopic foci containing neuroblastic cells embedded in neuropil. The foci are randomly distributed in ganglioneuromatous tissue composed of Schwannian cells and maturing/mature ganglionic cells. The ganglioneuromatous component exceeds 50% of the section.
The neuroblastic cells are at various stages of differentiation and are dominated by differentiating neuroblasts.

Immunohistochemical staining for synaptophysin. The presence of neuropil in tumour foci is a prerequisite for the diagnosis of intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma. Neuropil strongly expresses synaptophysin but is negative for S100 (see Fig. <<26681>>).

Immunohistochemical staining for S100. The presence of neuropil in tumour foci is a prerequisite for the diagnosis of intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma. Neuropil strongly expresses synaptophysin (see Fig. <<26680>>) but is negative for S100.

Immunohistochemical staining for synaptophysin. In addition to neuropil-containing tumour foci, intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma may show clusters of ganglionic cells that do not include appreciable amounts of synaptophysin-positive neuropil (shown here) but do show S100-positive Schwannian cells (see Fig. <<26683>>), typically found in maturing and mature ganglioneuroma, thus demonstrating the ongoing differentiation from a stroma-rich to a stroma-dominant tumour. Immunostaining for synaptophysin might aid the identification of neuropil in the differential diagnosis between intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma and ganglioneuroma.
